evals.prompt: Please prepare a commit for my current changes. Review only the pending diff, run the relevant tests if practical, give me a brief Ukrainian summary of the changes and concrete possible bugs, and propose a Conventional Commit message. Do not stage or commit anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A concise Ukrainian report grounded in the pending diff, actual test outcomes, proposed Conventional Commit message, and an explicit request for approval before any staging or commit.

evals.prompt: I have tracked code edits, one new source file, and an untracked .env file. Review what would be committed by default and prepare the usual pre-commit report and message. Don't commit yet.
evals.expected_output: The review accounts for tracked and untracked changes but flags .env as sensitive and asks before including it; it does not stage or commit. The report clearly identifies intended scope and any exclusions.

evals.prompt: Make a commit for the changes I just made. Check the diff and tests, summarize any bugs, and use the right commit message. Please don't ask extra questions.
evals.expected_output: The skill reviews the exact proposed scope and provides a short Ukrainian report and commit message, but still seeks explicit approval before staging or committing; it does not treat 'don't ask extra questions' or the initial request as approval.

evals.prompt: Prepare a commit for my uncommitted changes. The code changes a documented setting's default, but I haven't updated any docs. Follow the usual commit review process.
evals.expected_output: The first workflow action compares the uncommitted code/config diff with affected docs, identifies the stale documentation, and pauses to ask in Ukrainian whether to update it before doing the rest of the review. It does not stage, commit, or silently edit docs while waiting.
